rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Statement 5: Corollary or consequence of Straight line: length of perpendicular from a given point to a given line, bisectors of the angles between two straight lines  ·  **Acute vs obtuse.** The two bisectors are perpendicular; when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ < 0 the '+' combination bisects the acute angle, and when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ > 0 it bisects the obtuse angle.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Bisector equations.** The angle bisectors of the lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 are (a₁x + b₁y + c₁)/√(a₁² + b₁²) = ± (a₂x + b₂y + c₂)/√(a₂² + b₂²).  ·  **Equal distance property.** Any point on a bisector is equidistant from the two lines, using the perpendicular distance |ax + by + c|/√(a² + b²).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Recall the formula for Angle Bisector — Worked Example (a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ method).  ·  Recall the formula for Angle Bisector Between Two Lines — The a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ Rule.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Worked steps.** Write both equations in general form, divide each by the square root of the sum of its squared coefficients, combine with ±, and simplify each result.  ·  **Use of the result.** The bisector equations locate the in-centre of a triangle (intersection of internal bisectors) and solve locus problems requiring equal distance from two lines.
